10390.body:
This PR proposes to build Torch separately for `cpu, cuda and rocm`. For now torch-rocm is not enabled as it requires full distribution of rocm (nearly 11GB)[a]. We should be able to build most/all of [a] from sources using https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-libraries . 

For now this PR proposes to split torch in cpu and cuda part as a proof of concept that we can dynamically select env depending on available resources. Currently this PR proposes the following
- `py3-torch`: Only cpu c++ API and python interface
- `py3-torch-cuda`: cuda and cpu  c++ API and python interface
- `py3-torch-<extensions>` (e.g. `cluster`, `scatter` and `sparse`): cpu only python interface
- `py3-torch-<extensions>-cuda` (e.g. `cluster`, `scatter` and `sparse`): cuda and cpu python interface

As we do not have `py3-torch-rocm` yet ( which needs full 11GB of rocm distribution), on amdgpu hosts we fall back to cpu only interface. SCRAM will dynamically set the env e.g. on
- cpu only host:
  - LD_LIBRARY_PATH: `<path>/lib`
  - PYTHON3PATH:`<path>/lib/python3.12/site-packages`
- host with cuda:
  - LD_LIBRARY_PATH: `<path>/lib/scram_cuda:<path>/lib`(where <path>/lib/scram_cuda contains libs for cuda and cpu torch)
  - PYTHON3PATH: `<path>/lib/python3.12/site-packages/scram_cuda:<path>/lib/python3.12/site-packages`

for rocm, for now we fall back to cpu only libs/python modules.

I also have added triton and aotriton spec so that if we have to build the torch-rocm fully from sources then we can use aotirton. For now torch-rocm downloads prebuild aotriton bundle at build time

This need https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw-config/pull/117 too

51736.author: ljuckett
51736.body: ## Description Previously in phase 2 tk DQM histograms could only easily be booked at the top level (whole IT or OT) or the "deepest" level (individual rings, wheels, and layers). This PR adds a way to book histograms at every "depth" of the tracker without having to manually navigate folder structure or create extra if statements at the filling stage. ## "Depth" system When booking a histogram, the depth must be specified. By default, histograms will be booked at every depth. ``` if (bookingDepth == ENDCAP_WHEEL) { local_mes.XY_byWheel = phase2tkutil::book2DFromPSet(config_.getParameter("XY_byWheel"), ibooker, prettyName); } ``` When booking the histogram, the depth or substructure does not need to be checked. It only needs to be checked that _the histogram exists_ (and, if applicable, the module type). ``` if (local_mes.XY_byWheel) local_mes.XY_byWheel->Fill(gx, gy); ``` There are 6 depth levels corresponding to different structures, represented by an enum in phase2tkutil: | Depth | Inner Tracker Structure | Outer Tracker Structure | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | InnerTracker | OuterTracker | | 2 | Barrel, forward, or endcap | Barrel or endcap | | 3 | Shell/Half-cylinder | (Endcaps only) Side | | 4 | (Endcaps only) Ring | (Endcaps only) Ring | | 5 | (Endcaps only) Wheel | (Endcaps only) Wheel | | 6 | Barrel layer OR ring in wheel | Barrel layer OR ring in wheel | `enum Depths { WHOLE_TK = 1, SUBSTRUCTURE, SHELL, ENDCAP_RING, ENDCAP_WHEEL, LAYER };` Three new histograms have been added to ITClusters that use the depth system: ``` MonitorElement* ClusterPos_Mod_Ladder = nullptr; // Only in Barrel and LAYER std::vector XY_byWheel; // Only in Endcap and SUBSTRUCTURE std::vector ClusterPos_BLayer_Mod_Ladder; // Only in Barrel and SUBSTRUCTURE ``` ## getHistoId This function replaces the previous getITHistoId, getOTHistoId, getITHistoWheelId, and getOTHistoWheelId. It gets either the filepath or "pretty name" for a detid. The function gets all the postition data (Substructure, side, layer, etc) and uses the depth to figure out which parts to include in the output. Note that the topFolder of "InnerTracker" or "OuterTracker" is determined by the individual DQM plugins, so the filepath output should be appended to that. Example filepath output, depth 4: > /Endcaps/EndcapPix/mI/Ring1 Example pretty output, depth 4: > IT endcap EPix shell mI Ring1 The pretty output can be used in histogram titles to make sharing screenshots of histograms more helpful: ## General changes 1. Improved some histogram labels & removed params for unused histograms 2. Used phase2tkutil parameter set & booking functions where possible 3. Removed CRACK-specific plugin config files, CRACK config is now in "regular" config files - Due to a change in pset handling, histograms are switched off/on in these configs instead of in the plugins themselves 5. Overhaul of TTCluster and TTStub to handle histograms in the same way as other TkDQM plugins 6. "Counter" histograms now work more intuitively 7. Fixed some bugs and removed magic numbers 8. Validation: removed uses of old getITHistoID and getOTHistoID + minor change to hardcoded filenames for compatibility (no other changes) ## DQM output size increase of a lot But it is necessary to be able to monitor at every level. DQM/Validation full output is [here](https://cernbox.cern.ch/s/glmaSCMu9gM3pAw)
51736.title: Tracker DQM: Add histogram booking at multiple levels

51829.author: felicepantaleo
51829.body:
The truth graph holds the full history of a simulated event. PR #51716 added truth levels to it. A level is a named rule that decides which particles count as truth objects. Examples are the particles that reach the calorimeter, or the hadrons that carry a b quark. A level never holds a particle together with one of its own ancestors, so the same energy is never counted twice. This PR adds the layer that compares reconstruction against those truth objects, and the DQM package that plots the result.

Any efficiency or fake rate needs one decision first: which truth object should a given reconstructed object correspond to. This PR answers that question with detector hits. A truth object owns the simulated hits of its particle and of every descendant of that particle. A reconstructed object owns the hits or the clusters that built it. The association compares the two sets of hits and gives a score in each direction. One score says how much of the reconstructed object the truth object explains. The other score says how much of the truth object the reconstructed object recovers.

The harder question is which truth object to compare with, and the answer depends on the event. Take a neutral pion that decays to two photons. If the two photons stay separate in the detector, the right truth objects are the two photons. If reconstruction merges them into one object, then no single photon explains that object, and the right truth object is the pion. A fixed choice of level is therefore wrong for one of the two cases.

This PR resolves that with an adaptive search. The search starts at the truth object that matches directly. It then moves up the decay chain while the larger truth object still explains the reconstructed object, and it stops where the match is best. In the example above it stops at the photon in the first case and at the pion in the second case. Each reconstructed object gets its own answer.

The search is exposed as working points. `Fixed` does not move up the chain at all. `AdaptiveTight` and `AdaptiveNominal` allow a small and a larger amount of climbing. One property makes these working points easy to interpret: a working point changes which truth object an object matches, never whether it matches at all. The set of reconstructed objects with a match is therefore the same at every working point. The fake rate does not move, and any change in purity measures the truth definition alone.

The PR provides these associations for tracks, tracksters, primary vertices, secondary vertices and the particle-flow clusters of the barrel calorimeters, one domain per subdetector. For each input collection it writes one reconstruction-to-truth map per working point, and one truth-to-reconstruction map. A shared producer computes the truth targets once per event, so the cost does not grow with the number of associator modules. Every Run4 era carries the enableTruth modifier, so the associators, the validators and the harvesters are scheduled in every Run4 relval through globalValidation and postValidation. The cost is the 0.89 s per event measured below, and the step4 memory the bot reports comes from the monitor elements this validation books. A customise is for a job that also wants the maps in its output, and a second one schedules the HLT twins, which no standard sequence schedules.

The DQM package turns those maps into the standard plots. For every collection it books the truth-driven metrics, the efficiency and the duplicate and split rates, once per truth level, and the reco-driven metrics, the fake rate, the purity and the pile-up rate, once per working point. The axes are transverse momentum, pseudorapidity, the calorimeter-entrance pseudorapidity, azimuth, the size of the truth object, its production position and impact parameter, its depth in the graph and the fraction of its footprint that belongs to the root particle. Each row is booked again per acceptance band, and a domain lists the bands it can populate. Because the truth level is an axis rather than a fixed choice, the same job answers the same question at several definitions of truth, and the plots can be read side by side. This is also what makes the association layer reviewable: an efficiency that moves when only the truth definition changes is visible immediately.

The PR also repairs two defects in code that #51716 merged. That PR removed the truncation parameters from the two graph dumpers but left the parameters in the configurations, so those modules fail parameter validation today. More important, a cycle in the graph could empty a truth level in silence, because the rule that removes covered members lets a member of a cycle remove itself. An empty level looks exactly like an event with no such particle, so the code now detects a cycle and reports it. Two smaller fixes prevent an index from wrapping past the end of a hit array, and stop the dumper from reporting energies against the wrong hits when an input collection is absent.

### Validation

The measured numbers below each state their sample.

The adaptive search works as intended on tracks. On 200 TenTau events without pileup, the purity of the truth match rises from 0.34 at `Fixed` to 0.86 at `AdaptiveNominal`, while the fake rate stays the same, as the construction requires. The whole associator chain costs 0.89 s per event on ttbar at PU200, measured on 10 events; the shared target producer costs 12.5 ms of that.

The truth side was verified on ten generator presets, with one sample per preset and 10 events per sample, on Run4 D122. The presets cover particle guns, single resonances, vector boson fusion, gluon fusion, top pairs, single top, dibosons, associated Higgs production, heavy flavour and inclusive QCD. Across 103 event graphs, every stored level bit agrees with a fresh recomputation, and the graph shows no cycle, no orphan fragment and no particle with more than one production vertex. A separate script reads the published graph files and repeats the check with its own code: no level ever holds a particle and one of its ancestors, a subgraph always holds at least the hits and the energy of the particle itself, and no neutrino carries hits.

The physics numbers are correct sample by sample. Top pair events give two b hadrons and two top quarks. Associated Higgs production gives two b hadrons from the H to bb decay, and single top gives one. Vector boson fusion gives six hard-process legs, which are the two tagging quarks and the four neutrinos, and no b hadron. Higgs to two photons gives two hard-process legs. Inclusive QCD names no resonance, so it has no signal level, and it still has 351 reconstructable final-state objects per event.

One caveat on the heavy-flavour sample. The standard `BsToMuMu` fragment states a filter efficiency of 1.38e-3, so ten accepted events are too expensive for this campaign. The heavy-flavour preset was therefore verified on the top-pair sample, where it seeds on hadron flavour and finds the expected b hadrons. The preset is verified; that particular fragment is not.

The branch builds on its own and passes all fourteen unit test suites. The DQM configuration constructs its 26 modules and sequences in a job.

### Notes

The pile-up record keeps the species in `collapsedGenKeptPdgIds` (pi0 by default), each on its own decay vertex, so `reconstructableFinalState` counts a pile-up pi0 as one object as it does a signal pi0. A GEN-only particle with no generator payload takes the summed momentum of the products of its own decays.

Every GEN-only vertex carries a reason: `HardScatter`, `ShowerBranching`, `Hadronization`, or `Decay`, read from the species and the generator status codes of the particles that meet there. The reason axis of the DQM plots is one bin per `VertexReason`, so the content of every `*_reason` histogram under `TruthInfo/` moves against the baseline, and a new folder `TruthInfo/Graph` holds nine monitor elements that summarise the graph per interaction. Both are expected differences in the comparison.

The interface gains a python reader (`PhysicsTools/TruthInfo/python/graphTools.py`), provenance accessors on every node (`bunchCrossing`, `eventIndex`, `isSignal`, `isFromPileup`, `hasMomentum`), a name for every enum, `branchesAtLevel`, allocation-free navigation, a JSON output of the graph dumper, and one worked analysis per selection preset in python and in C++ under `PhysicsTools/TruthInfo/test/`.

The five DQM validators of the first generation, their two association-map producers, the validation and harvesting configurations and the plot scripts move from `PhysicsTools/TruthInfo` to `Validation/TruthInfo`, so `PhysicsTools/TruthInfo` links no DQM code. The first-generation `BranchRecoValidator`, its two harvesters and its opt-in sequence are removed: `TruthBranchRecoValidator` books the same plots with the truth level and the working point as axes.

The shared-energy metric weights every cell by its reconstructed energy, as the TICL associators do. `BranchHitAssociator` takes a table of rechit energy per cell; the reconstructed object owns its cluster fraction of that energy, the truth object owns its simulated fraction of it, and a cell with a rechit and no simulated hit counts against the reconstructed object. The trackster associator reads the HGCAL rechits and the barrel PFRecHits the layer clusters are built from. Without a table, as in the unit tests and in the legacy-object validators, the weight is the total simulated energy of the cell.

The inner-tracker truth is keyed by cell. A tracker DetId names a module, so two particles crossing one module share every DetId they leave there, and at PU200 that is the dominant source of wrong track matches. The digi sim links name the cell each particle fired and a cluster names the same cells on the reco side, so the index carries the digi channel in the `recHitIndex` field, which the tracker channel never used: the persisted format is unchanged. The match is on the exact cell, so an index keyed by module alone matches no track: a file digitised before the tracker truth carried cells has to be reprocessed from the DIGI step, and the producer says so once per job. Measured on 20 ttbar events at PU200, both granularities on the same tracks and the same index, the match agrees with `QuickTrackAssociatorByHits` for 99.54% of the tracks by cell against 93.21% by module, and lands on an unrelated particle 0.04% of the time against 5.50%; above 10 GeV, where the jet cores are, 88.2% against 69.1%. Per event the index grows from 18.3 MB to 21.8 MB uncompressed and from 8.26 MB to 9.12 MB on disk, and the association costs no more time.

The adaptive search answers only with detector particles. A candidate root carries the hits of its whole subgraph, so a parton, a beam particle or a node the graph invents covers a reco object entirely and wins on score alone. `TruthBranchTargetsProducer` publishes `assignableRoots`, the candidate roots that are detector particles, and an adaptive working point answers only with those: the synthetic nodes, a particle with no production vertex, the partons and the W, the Z and the Higgs are barred, each behind its own flag. The vertex a particle was produced at is deliberately not a criterion: a preset attaches a real gun particle or a stable spectator to an artificial source vertex, and those are particles a detector sees. The barred roots stay candidates and stay in the first working point's map, because they are the members of the hard-process and parton-jet denominators and the truth-driven direction reads its pair scores from that map. On 20 ttbar events at PU200 the rule bars 10 to 14 roots per event out of about 13000 and moves 4.1% of the tracks from a hard-process ancestor to the particle they came from; every level denominator is unchanged.

Two defects found on a PU200 run are repaired. The mixed truth graph gave every pileup particle a signal particle's momentum and position, because the logical graph producer at DIGI read the signal SimTracks by bare trackId and the signal HepMC by barcode; the accumulator now emits every sub-event's SimTracks and SimVertices with their sub-event id, and the producer reads them by (event id, trackId). On ttbar at PU200 the stored pt of the particle behind a track was 0.58 of the track pt at the median before and is 0.997 after. Equal association scores, which every ancestor of a particle produces, were resolved by the lowest particle id and handed the first row of a map to an ancestor; they now rank by the tightest branch. The legacy validators key their TrackingParticle and CaloParticle lookups by event id and trackId, which a bare trackId cannot do at pileup. A study analyzer, `Validation/TruthInfo/test/TrackAssociationComparison.cc`, compares the track association with `QuickTrackAssociatorByHits` track by track.

One more defect in merged code is repaired: every truth configuration read the `Cleaned` instance of the barrel PFRecHit producers, which holds the hits that failed the quality tests. The rechit map, the dumper, the calorimeter validator and the configurations now read the plain instance.


The DQM package is included here rather than in a later PR, because the association maps and the truth targets have no other consumer, and a reviewer cannot judge the association layer without seeing what it plots.

Energy sums and scores use `double` deliberately. The sums of squares span keV squared to TeV squared, and the reverse score subtracts two large and nearly equal terms. Quantities that do not accumulate use `float`.

Some commits change code that #51716 merged rather than the new association layer. They are here because one configuration fails today and the level defect is silent.

52134.author: CMS-HGCAL
52134.body:
#### PR description:

This PR relates to this issue https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/issues/51938

Spurious alignment of relative high energy deposits (PCaloHits) repeated frequently may lead to a very high charge deposit localized in a single cell. In this regime TOT is triggered and a loop is used to estimate the total integration time.
The total integration time is parameterized as a quadratic function: without a protection on the max charge allowed it may potentially enter in a non-defined regime. 

The fix consists in forcing all bunches that follow the one with charge above the TOT saturation to be declared as busy and the iterative loop for the estimation of the integration time to stop.

Phase-2 : No back port needed.

#### PR validation:

The PR was validated under the conditions of issue https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/issues/51938
52134.title: Fix: [HGCAL] Adding upstream protection for saturated TOT charge

52158.author: fwyzard
52158.body: #### PR description: This PR partially addresses #52253. Currently every module call copies the job's `ServiceToken` (a `std::shared_ptr`), or locks a `ServiceWeakToken` to it, and release it again: in `Path::runNextWorkerAsync` / `workerFinished`, in the worker tasks, in every `ServiceRegistry::Operate`. All threads of the job therefore update the same atomic reference count, whose cache line bounces between cores and sockets; on large two-socket machines this is a bottleneck for the whole job. This PR makes `ServiceToken` a non-owning handle to the services: a plain pointer, trivially copyable, with no reference counting. The ownership moves to a new `OwningServiceToken`, returned by `ServiceRegistry::createSet`, `createContaining` and `createServicesFromConfig`, and held by the owners of the services: `EventProcessor`, `TestProcessor`, `TestSourceProcessor`, `PythonEventProcessor`, `cmsRun`, `PileUp`, and the standalone tools and tests that create their own service set. `ServiceRegistry::Operate` and `presentToken()` are non-owning; the new `ServiceRegistry::LockedOperate` holds an `OwningServiceToken` and makes its services available. All the asynchronous tasks and callbacks (event paths, workers, transforms, stream and global transitions, EventSetup callbacks, delayed reader) capture the caller's `ServiceToken` instead of a `ServiceWeakToken`. `ServiceWeakToken` is renamed `WeakServiceToken`, and remains for objects that can outlive the services, e.g. the `TFile` of `TStorageFactoryFile`. The `OwningServiceToken` is passed down the construction of a service set: the `EventProcessor`, `TestProcessor` and `TestSourceProcessor` constructors take one, `ScheduleItems::initServices` and `addTNS` update it in place, and `ServiceRegistry::createSet` / `createContaining` take the base service set as an `OwningServiceToken`, whose `ServicesManager` the new one keeps alive. A `ServicesManager` can only be created by `ServicesManager::create()`, which builds it in a `std::shared_ptr` and only then creates its services, so that a service can take an owning or a weak token to its own service set in its constructor. `ServicesManager` derives from `std::enable_shared_from_this` only so that an owning or weak token can be obtained from a non-owning one, as `PileUp` and `TStorageFactoryFile` do. The `SourceCoordinator`, created before the services, holds a non-owning `ServiceToken` set once they exist. Behaviour changes for code outside the framework: - a `ServiceToken` must not outlive the `OwningServiceToken` that owns the services; it cannot be obtained from a temporary `OwningServiceToken` (compile-time error); - code that creates its own services must keep the result in an `OwningServiceToken` (`edm::ServiceToken token = edm::ServiceRegistry::createSet(...)` does not compile any more); this affects the standalone tools and the unit tests of `CondCore`, `FWStorage`, `HeterogeneousCore`, `PhysicsTools` and `FWCore`, updated here; - the `EventProcessor`, `TestProcessor` and `TestSourceProcessor` constructors, and `createSet` / `createContaining` with a base service set, take an `OwningServiceToken` instead of a `ServiceToken`; - `ServiceWeakToken` is renamed `WeakServiceToken`, and its `lock()` returns an `OwningServiceToken`; - `setupSiteLocalConfig()` returns a `ServiceRegistry::LockedOperate` that owns the service it makes available; - `connect` and `copySlotsTo` are only available on `OwningServiceToken`; `connectTo` and `copySlotsFrom` are removed from the tokens (they were unused); - a `ServicesManager` can only be created with `ServicesManager::create()`, which returns a `std::shared_ptr`; only the `ServiceRegistry` and its unit tests did this; - the module-facing `doTransformAsync` / `transformAsync_` take a `ServiceToken const&` instead of a `ServiceWeakToken const&`; no module outside `FWCore/Framework` implements them. This replaces the earlier version of this PR, which kept the owning token and added a separate `ServiceRegistry::OperateNonOwning` with tokens passed by reference to the tasks, following the [suggestion](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/52158#issuecomment-6200819862) by @Dr15Jones. Making the non-owning handle the default removes the second `Operate`, the reference-lifetime conventions in the tasks, and the changes to `ESProductResolverTemplate`, for the same performance. ##### Measurements HLT menu `/online/collisions/2026/2e34/v1.3/HLT/V2`, run 402360 HLTPhysics data read with `DAQSource` from local FRD files, CPU only, jobs pinned with `taskset` to N cores and both of their SMT siblings (threads = streams = cpus), 2 concurrent lumisections, 4 repetitions per point, average standard deviation. Throughput from the `ThroughputService` over at least 60 s per job. Scaling with the number of cores on a 2 AMD EPYC 9655 machine (2 96 Zen 5 cores; the container leaves out one core per socket, so a full socket has 95 cores and the full machine 190), cores added in order, `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-23-1100` with and without this PR. The dashed line is the IB extrapolated linearly from one full CCD (8 cores), so the L3 sharing within a CCD is not counted as a loss. The left plot shows the throughput as measured, the right one the throughput normalised to 3.0 GHz, the clock frequency observed when the full machine is in use: The IB stops scaling at about 64-95 cores (446.3 2.3 ev/s with 190 cores, at 3.77 GHz); with this PR the throughput keeps growing to the full machine (772.4 0.2 ev/s at 2.97 GHz, +73%). At a fixed clock it follows the extrapolation from one CCD, within 1.5%, up to about 80 cores, and reaches 90% of it on the full machine. One job on all the cores of the machine, compared with concurrent jobs each pinned to one socket or to one CCD (`CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-23-1100`, average standard deviation of 4 repetitions, ev/s): | 2 EPYC 9655 | IB | this PR | | |---|---|---|---| | one job, 190 cores | 447.2 3.9 | 771.7 2.7 | +72.6% 1.6% | | two jobs, one per socket (95 cores each) | 761.5 0.6 | 845.6 1.2 | +11.0% 0.2% | | 24 jobs, one per CCD (8 cores each) | 869.5 0.3 | 871.6 0.2 | +0.2% 0.1% | With the previous version of this PR (`CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-19-1100`, 3 repetitions), on two other machines: | machine | one job, all cores: IB | previous version | | two jobs, one per socket: IB | previous version | | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 2 EPYC 9534 (124 cores) | 311.2 2.4 | 391.4 4.9 | +25.8% 1.8% | 435.4 0.4 | 436.7 2.6 | +0.3% 0.6% | | 2 EPYC 9965 (382 cores) | 410 1 | 502 16 | +22.4% 3.9% | 852.7 0.5 | 1306.2 1.9 | +53.2% 0.2% | On the 9965 this PR improves all results, but the single full-machine job remains far below the two per-socket jobs. This will be addressed separately. #### PR validation: As of 80d202dbb31ffaa2dfd51f1ac1574528b1ac502c all unit tests pass, and the matrix workflows run without issues. The final version of the PR was tested in 267 benchmark jobs on the 2 EPYC 9655 (the socket configurations, the scan over the number of cores and the perf checks above); all of them completed successfully. A previous version of this PR was also tested on two other machines (2 EPYC 9534, 2 EPYC 9965): the HLT gave identical decisions on 4000 events (16 threads, no prescales), and all benchmarks ran without encountering any issues.
52158.title: Rework the Services ownership to improve scaling to large number of cores

52166.author: GNiendorf
52166.body:
#### Summary
  LST memory per event drops by about 75%, with no timing cost and no change in physics.

  #### Memory: LST peak per event (one event at a time)
Base: `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-12-1100` plus the T5/T4 DNN retrain (merged in cms-sw after that IB). "master" is that base; "this PR" is the base plus this PR rebased onto it (outputs bit-identical to the base with strict FP). Standalone, CPU.

  | Sample | master | this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | ttbar, PU200 (100 events) | 96.3 MB | 22.3 MB (-77%) |
  | QCD high-pT jets, no pileup (50 events) | 27.7 MB | 9.8 MB (-65%) |

  GPU (L40):
  - `lst_cuda` process peak, 1 / 4 streams: 912 / 1418 MiB -> 576 / 701 MiB. Note that this includes 444 MiB of fixed CUDA memory unrelated to LST.
  - Phase-2 HLT, 16 jobs x 16 threads/streams, ttbar PU200: 41.8 -> 37.4 GB in total (-275 MiB per job), measured earlier before the DNN retrain PR.

  **Pixel tracking now holds most of the remaining GPU memory pool.**

  #### What changed
  1. **Compaction after creation.** The counting kernels are unchanged. Objects are created into a short-lived buffer sized by the count, then copied into a collection of exactly the produced size, and the buffer is freed (segments, triplets, quintuplets, quadruplets, pT3, pT5).
  2. **Buffers freed after their last use.** Hits after the MD stage; build-only columns after their stage.
  3. **Counts and overflow.** The T3 and T5 counts apply one cut that creation always applies to reduce buffer size.
  4. **CMSSW.** The TrackingRecHit pointers become a host-only product of LSTInputProducer. LSTInputProducer no longer copies the input pixel seeds: it publishes references to them, which LSTOutputConverter reads (its `lstPixelSeeds` parameter is removed), and the Tier0 seed monitor merges initialStepSeeds and highPtTripletStepSeeds itself.
  5. **Standalone.** The SoACommon stand-in in `bin/lst.cc` is updated to the current SoA API.
  6. **Atomics.** Counters updated from more than one block now use device-wide atomics (a pre-existing bug, fixed in a separate commit).

  #### Timing (standalone LST ttbar PU200)
  | | master | this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | CPU, 32 streams | 33.43 ms/event | 33.28 ms/event |
  | GPU (L40), 4 streams | 2.145 ms/event | 2.062 ms/event |

  HLT throughput is unchanged.

  #### Validation
  MTV, 500 ttbar + 500 QCD (pT-hat 1.8-2.4 TeV) events, PU200, CPU, `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-12-2300` vs the same IB + this PR: Phase-2 HLT, and offline (workflow 34634.711, with and without trackingIters01): https://gniendorf.github.io/lst-plots/pr280/

c.c. @slava77

52208.author: AuroraPerego
52208.body:
#### PR description:

Calling the `sort()` method on a `mapWithSharedEnergy`/`mapWithFraction` leads to a compile-time error.
The reason is that the `sort()` method in the `TICLAssociationMap` is missing `constexpr` in the `if (byScore && IsValueTypeWithScore<V>::value)`, leading to the block of code within this `if` being always compiled. However, in those two cases, `score()` is not defined and the compilation fails.

This PR guards that block of code with `if (constexpr IsValueTypeWithScore<V>::value)`, leaving the `if (byScore)` check at runtime. It also adds a `requires is_one_to_one` to methods that work only with one-to-one maps, but nothing prevented them from being called with one-to-many. 
I also added the test that I used to check all methods in the `TICLAssociationMap`.

#### PR validation:

The new test added passes.

52213.author: bfonta
52213.body:
Set of minor improvements on the `PFBlock` linking (weighted quick union) algorithm: 

+ Avoid multiple calls to `.size()`
+ Avoid additional calls to `.type()`, including moving the definition of `type1` to its corresponding outer loop
+ Remove duplicated logic when computing the distance between two elements in the (removed) `links()` method
+ Remove a spurious parent assignment in the `unite()` method of the weighted quick union, which can lead to a cycle in the node chain if `p` is a root node. The cycle was broken by the `find` function (path halving), leading AFAICT to correct results, but the implementation was not precise in the general case (and included extra instructions). I thus removed the `id_[p] = q;` line in `PFBlockAlgo::unite()`.
+ Add a `if` check in `unite()` for when the two nodes are already connected (they have the same root node); the code was formally wrong but without any impact due to `connected()` call before `unite()` in `findBlocks`, which prevents nodes with the same root to arrive to `unite()`.
+ The storage of the root notes in the `keys` vector was simplified and accelerated.
+ The code was reserving a number of blocks equal to the number of elements, while we only need to reserve a number equal to the root nodes, since each root node leads to one block.

The logic and essential structure of the algorithm is unchanged.
52213.title: PFBlockAlgo improvements.

52279.author: fwyzard
52279.body:
#### PR description:

The `FastTimerService` registers each thread when it enters the TBB arena it observes. A thread that reaches one of its signals without having entered that arena (_e.g._ a thread running in another task_arena, or outside of TBB) was not registered, and timing it dereferenced a null pointer.

The `FastTimerService` now registers those threads on their first measurement, and reports how many there have been at the end of the job.

A new unit test, `UnobservedThreadSignals`, emits the delayed-get signals of a module from a new `std::thread`, which has never entered a TBB arena. Without these changes the job crashes; now it passes and reports the three unobserved threads at the end of the job.

As a minor optimisation, the number of calls to read the per-thread data with `::pthread_getspecific()` has been reduced to one per measurement.


#### PR validation:

The new unit test passes.
52279.title: `FastTimerService`: handle unknown threads

52291.author: sbaldu
52291.body:
#### PR description:
`BarrelCLUEAlgo` currently iterates over the search box in `calculateLocalDensity` and `calculateDistanceToHigher` with a strict `<` sign. However, `searchBox` returns inclusive bin ranges. This makes it skip the last row and column of tiles for each search box.
This PR includes both extremes of the search box in the loop.
52291.title: Fix search box comparison in BarrelCLUEAlgo

52292.author: makortel
52292.body:
#### PR description:

The first test of RNTuple RelVals reported Merge job failures https://gitlab.cern.ch/cms-ppd/monitoring-operation/special-relvals-requests/-/work_items/313#note_12613491 . Those failures are presumably caused by the Merge job trying to merge TTree files. To address the situation this PR adds an `nrtuple` configuration option to the Merge jobs.

This PR also adds a rudimentary unit test that checks the Source and OutputModule types for various configuration option combinations.

Note: I don't know what kind of interaction needs to happen between workflow submission, WM, and the `Merge.py` in order to enable the `rntuple` option.

Resolves https://github.com/cms-sw/framework-team/issues/2471

#### PR validation:

Unit tests succeed.
52292.title: Add rntuple option to Merge jobs, add rudimentary unit test
